fixedAt: 2026-10-26, before any real-model generation for this evaluation
scope: /hey csinterview (2 questions) and /hey morecs (up to 4) real GMS outputs
scale: 1-5 per question; 5, 3 and 1 are anchored below, 4 and 2 sit between

coreDepth.5: A must-know fundamental the change truly relies on, asked one layer below the definition (why it holds, when it breaks, cost, interplay)
coreDepth.3: A fundamental, but the question stops at 'what is the right approach?'
coreDepth.1: Unrelated to the change or a surface fact

nonNiche.5: Textbook fundamental; nothing to look up
nonNiche.3: Vendor/API wording appears but the answer does not depend on it
nonNiche.1: Decided by a vendor flag, exact number, API behaviour, repository rule or rare edge case

knowledgeApplication.5: Both a candidate lacking the concept and one who only knows its definition pick a wrong option
knowledgeApplication.3: Filters only one of the two
knowledgeApplication.1: Solvable by name/definition matching or elimination of strawmen

uniqueAnswer.5: The stated conditions determine exactly one option
uniqueAnswer.3: Needs one unstated but reasonable assumption
uniqueAnswer.1: Two or more options are defensible

distractors.5: All three wrong options are real, common misconceptions

learningValue.5: Explanation teaches name (Korean+English), definition/mechanism, application and when the conclusion changes; wrong-option notes name the confused concept
learningValue.1: Restates the code or the answer

grounding.5: Anchor location is where the change relies on the concept; facts and assumptions are separated correctly

anchorFit.5: One layer below the anchor's concept and solvable without the anchor's answer

newQuestionJustified.5: New interview question covers an uncovered core concept that beats the remaining follow-ups; or 4+0 was the right call
newQuestionJustified.3: Core but a follow-up would have taught more

noDrift.5: Later rounds stay at general-principle scope

binaryChecks.bareDefinition: Question is answered by picking a name or definition
binaryChecks.ambiguous: More than one option defensible under the stated conditions

procedure: Each sample: csinterview with the previous prompt (25312d1, 5 questions) as 'before', the new csinterview as 'after', then 3 chained /hey morecs. Score every after/morecs question; score before questions on the same dimensions for comparison. Prompt changes are allowed at most 3 times and each is logged with its reason.
